roadmap.goal: Fix ADO Bug #6068. The calver build counter in .github/workflows/ci_version.yml emits v<YY>.<M>.<D>.0 on roughly 1 in 7 push runs to main, because github.rest.actions.listWorkflowRuns intermittently returns a stale page whose newest run already predates today's midnight, so the counting loop breaks on its first iteration with buildCount === 0. A second, deterministic defect makes every pull_request run emit .0, because context.ref.replace('refs/heads/','') leaves the literal refs/pull/<N>/merge, which matches no branch. Both are fixed by asserting the one invariant the script can check: the current run is itself a ci.yml run created today, so it MUST appear in the result set. The logic is extracted to a testable ES module first, because it is currently an inline YAML string with no test harness and no regression test can bind to it.

validation.notes: Three-step roadmap for a CI defect whose fix is fully specified by the corrected RCA (docs/feature/fix-build-version-always-zero/rca.md section 0) and approved by the maintainer. Step 01-01 extracts the CURRENT buggy logic verbatim and writes the regression tests, which go RED — the bug surviving extraction is what proves the extraction faithful. Step 01-02 applies the fix and turns them GREEN. Step 01-03 wires the workflow to the module and runs the tests in CI. No solution-architect dispatch: /nw-bugfix prescribes a minimal roadmap and the RCA already specifies the fix at diff level, so re-deriving it would add no information. Prior-wave artifacts (feature-delta.md, DISTILL .feature files) do not exist for this bugfix — the RCA is the authoritative input, per /nw-bugfix Phase 3.

ssot_inputs.architecture_brief: docs/product/architecture/brief.md (consulted: zero matches for ci_version / calver / fileversion / build version — this change is entirely outside the application architecture SSOT, so no component-inventory update is owed)

out_of_scope: Root cause C — concurrent main runs read the same count and collide (v26.9.21.3 emitted at 05:42:03 AND 05:42:08; .7 at 05:49:44 AND 05:50:54). This is a reservation-vs-read defect that needs a maintainer decision on the versioning scheme (run_number in the 4th segment, abandoning 'Nth build of the day', versus restoring a tag-based reservation). Adding a concurrency: group does NOT fix it — serialising the query does not help when both runs read the same 'runs that exist' value. Raise as a separate ADO item.

Fix 4 from the RCA — rewriting todayStart as new Date(Date.UTC(...)). Not in the approved scope, and a provable no-op on hosted runners, which are UTC. Latent only for a non-UTC self-hosted runner. Leave the existing expression byte-for-byte when extracting.

Reverting bd8a2db60 — the maintainer's 'undo whatever changed this' was investigated and priced in RCA section 7. That commit also rewrote ci_changes.yml, rewired 72 lines of ci.yml and moved release tagging, with eight months of CI stacked on top, and its pre-change PR behaviour was a bare github.run_number, not calver. It is also not the cause of the reported intermittent defect. Forward fix only.

Mutation testing — CLAUDE.md sets per-feature strategy, but that names Stryker.NET for the C# backend and StrykerJS for the React frontend. Neither is configured for a standalone ES module under .github/scripts/, and wiring a third Stryker runner for ~60 lines of CI glue is disproportionate. Explicitly N/A with reason, not a silent skip. The test suite instead pins behaviour directly via injected stubs, which is the same property mutation testing would be probing.
Backfilling or re-tagging any release that already shipped with a .0 version. No such release exists (gh release list shows none, and the remote carries no such tag).

phases.name: Make the calver build counter trustworthy
phases.description: Extract the counting logic to a testable module with the bug intact (RED), fix it (GREEN), then wire the workflow to the module and run the tests in CI.

steps.name: Extract counting logic verbatim and pin the two defects with failing tests
steps.description:
TDD execution.

**RED phase** — Two new files.

(a) `.github/scripts/generate-version.mjs`. Move the counting logic out of the inline `script:` block in `.github/workflows/ci_version.yml` (lines 26-85) into an exported pure function with ALL I/O injected:

```js
export async function generateVersion({ listRuns, ref, pullRequestHeadRef, now, runId, sleep })
```

It returns `{ version, fileversion, buildCount }`. `listRuns` is an async function taking `{ branch, page }` and returning an array of run objects shaped `{ id, created_at }` — the real caller wraps `github.rest.actions.listWorkflowRuns`. `sleep` is injected so tests never actually wait.

This step is a FAITHFUL extraction: copy the existing date-prefix computation, the `todayStart` expression (leave it as the local-timezone `new Date(y, m, d)` — see out_of_scope), the branch derivation `ref.replace('refs/heads/', '')`, the pagination loop with its 10-page safety limit, the `runDate < todayStart` break and the `buildCount++`, and the `v${datePrefix}.${buildNumber}` formatting. Do NOT fix anything in this step. The bug must survive extraction — that is what proves the extraction faithful. Do not use `runId` or `pullRequestHeadRef` yet; accept them in the signature so step 01-02 has somewhere to put the fix.

(b) `.github/scripts/generate-version.test.mjs` using `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`. Five tests:

1. `counts the current run on a push to main` — `listRuns` returns a fresh page containing `runId` plus 3 earlier runs from today and several from previous days. Expect `buildCount === 4` and `version === 'v26.9.22.4'`. **This one PASSES against the unfixed code — it is the regression pin that proves the fix does not break the working path.**
2. `does not report zero when the API serves a stale page` — `listRuns` returns a page whose newest run is 16 days old and which does NOT contain `runId` (the observed failure: total_count drifted and workflow_runs[0].created_at came back as 2026-09-05 while today was 2026-09-22). Expect the call to REJECT rather than return a version. **RED** — unfixed code returns buildCount 0 and `v26.9.22.0`.
3. `derives the branch from the head ref on a pull_request` — `ref` is `'refs/pull/1777/merge'`, `pullRequestHeadRef` is `'dependabot/x'`. The stub returns runs ONLY when queried with `branch === 'dependabot/x'` and `[]` for anything else — exactly what the real API does. Expect `buildCount >= 1` and a version not ending in `.0`. **RED** — unfixed code queries `'refs/pull/1777/merge'`, gets `[]`, returns 0.
4. `retries until the current run becomes visible` — stub serves the stale page on calls 1 and 2 and a fresh page containing `runId` on call 3. Expect the correct count, and assert the stub was called 3 times so the retry is real and not incidental. **RED** — unfixed code never retries.
5. `fails loudly rather than emitting a .0 version` — stub is permanently stale. Assert it rejects, and assert that no return value ending in `.0` is ever produced. **RED**.

Run `node --test .github/scripts/` and CONFIRM test 1 passes and tests 2-5 fail, each for the stated reason, BEFORE writing any fix. Paste that output into the commit body.

**GREEN phase** — none in this step. Tests 2-5 stay RED; that is the deliverable. Do not touch `ci_version.yml` yet.

**COMMIT phase** — `test(ci): pin the calver build-counter defects with failing tests`. Body records the RED output and cites Bug #6068.

**COMMIT MUST BE GREEN — project rule.** This repository never commits or pushes a red suite (see CLAUDE.md quality gates and the green-before-push convention). So the RED state is *demonstrated and recorded*, then parked:

1. Write all 5 tests with NO skip markers.
2. Run `node --test .github/scripts/` and capture the output verbatim. It MUST show test 1 passing and tests 2-5 failing. Verify each failure's message matches its stated cause — a test failing on a typo or a bad import is NOT a RED state, it is a broken test.
3. Paste that captured output into the commit body. This is the evidence the bug survived extraction; it is the whole point of this step.
4. ONLY THEN mark tests 2-5 skipped, e.g. `test('...', { skip: 'RED until step 01-02 — Bug #6068' }, async () => {...})`. Do not alter a single line of their bodies while doing so.
5. Re-run `node --test .github/scripts/`. It must now report 1 passing, 4 skipped, 0 failing.
6. Commit in that state.

Step 01-02 removes those skip markers. Parking them is what keeps the tree green between the two commits without weakening the RED evidence.
steps.scenario_name: Regression pin for Bug #6068 — stale-page zero (intermittent, main) and pull_request ref mismatch (deterministic)
red_to_green_tests: counts the current run on a push to main (regression pin — passes pre-fix)
does not report zero when the API serves a stale page (RED)
derives the branch from the head ref on a pull_request (RED)
retries until the current run becomes visible (RED)
fails loudly rather than emitting a .0 version (RED)
criteria: `.github/scripts/generate-version.mjs` exists and exports `generateVersion({ listRuns, ref, pullRequestHeadRef, now, runId, sleep })`.

The extracted logic is behaviourally identical to the inline block in ci_version.yml — same date prefix, same todayStart expression, same branch derivation, same pagination and break condition, same version string format.
`.github/scripts/generate-version.test.mjs` exists with exactly the five named tests.
RED EVIDENCE: with no skip markers, `node --test .github/scripts/` reported 1 passing and 4 failing, and that raw output is pasted in the commit body.

Each of the 4 failures was verified to fail for its stated reason — asserted on the actual returned value (e.g. buildCount 0 / a version ending in `.0`), not merely that something threw. A failure from an import error, typo or bad stub does NOT count as RED.
COMMITTED STATE IS GREEN: tests 2-5 carry a skip marker naming step 01-02, their bodies otherwise unmodified, and `node --test .github/scripts/` reports 1 passing, 4 skipped, 0 failing.
ci_version.yml is NOT modified in this step.
Commit follows conventional commits with scope `ci`.

steps.name: Assert the current run is visible, retry, and fail loudly
steps.description:
TDD execution — turn tests 2-5 GREEN.

**GREEN phase** — Two files. First, in `.github/scripts/generate-version.test.mjs`, remove the skip markers that step 01-01 put on tests 2-5. Change NOTHING else in that file — no assertion, no stub, no test 1. Then edit `.github/scripts/generate-version.mjs`. Three changes:

1. **Branch fallback.** Derive the branch as `pullRequestHeadRef ?? ref.replace('refs/heads/', '')`. On a push `pullRequestHeadRef` is undefined and the expression is byte-for-byte the current behaviour, so the working path is untouched.

2. **Current-run visibility check.** While paginating, record whether any returned run has `id === runId` (compare loosely — the API returns a number, `context.runId` is a number, but be defensive about string/number mismatch). After the loop, if the current run was NOT seen, the listing is stale or the branch filter matched nothing — the count is meaningless. Retry the whole listing from page 1 with backoff. Use at least 5 attempts with a growing delay via the injected `sleep` (e.g. 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s, 32s), because the observed staleness lasted across consecutive calls.

3. **Fail loudly.** If the current run is still not visible after the final attempt, THROW with a diagnostic naming `buildCount`, the `branch` actually queried, `ref`, and `runId`. Never return a version. The caller maps this to `core.setFailed`. Rationale for failing rather than defaulting to 1: a wrong version can overwrite an already-pushed and cosign-signed ghcr.io tag, so a red build is strictly cheaper than a silently wrong version. This is the maintainer's explicit choice.

Do NOT change the date-prefix computation, the `todayStart` expression, the 10-page safety limit, or the version string format.

**Verification** — `node --test .github/scripts/` must report all 5 passing. Test 1 (the regression pin) must STILL pass, unmodified — if it needed changing, the fix altered the working path and is wrong.

**COMMIT phase** — `fix(ci): count builds only when the current run is visible`. Body cites Bug #6068, states the two defects fixed, and records the full green test output.
steps.scenario_name: Same five scenarios — all green after the fix
red_to_green_tests: does not report zero when the API serves a stale page
derives the branch from the head ref on a pull_request
retries until the current run becomes visible
fails loudly rather than emitting a .0 version
criteria: All 5 tests in generate-version.test.mjs pass — 5 passing, 0 skipped, 0 failing.

The ONLY change to generate-version.test.mjs is the removal of the skip markers from tests 2-5. `git diff` on that file shows no other edit: test 1 is untouched, and no assertion, stub or expected value anywhere was weakened to make a test pass.
Branch derivation is `pullRequestHeadRef ?? ref.replace('refs/heads/', '')` — the push path is byte-for-byte unchanged.
The function retries at least 5 times with backoff via the injected `sleep` before giving up.
On persistent staleness the function THROWS; it never returns a version ending in `.0`.
The thrown message names buildCount, the queried branch, ref, and runId.
The date prefix, todayStart expression, 10-page limit and version format are unchanged.
Commit follows conventional commits with scope `ci`.
deliverables: .github/scripts/generate-version.mjs (modified — branch fallback, run-visibility retry, loud failure)

steps.name: Wire the workflow to the module and run the tests in CI
steps.scenario_name: Workflow delegates to the tested module; tests gate the build
red_to_green_tests: all five module tests remain green after the workflow is rewired
criteria: ci_version.yml imports generate-version.mjs and no longer contains the counting loop inline.
The `workflow_call` outputs block still exposes exactly `version` and `fileversion` with the same meaning — no consumer of these outputs needs changing.
A thrown error from the module reaches `core.setFailed`, so the job goes red rather than emitting a version.
The five log lines operators recognise still appear in the job output.
ci.yml gained a job that runs `node --test .github/scripts/` and whose failure fails the build. No new workflow file was created.
Both modified YAML files parse cleanly.
`node --test .github/scripts/` is green.
Commit follows conventional commits with scope `ci`.

VERIFICATION LIMIT (state this in the commit body, do not overclaim): these tests prove the module's retry and branch-fallback logic against injected stubs. They do NOT reproduce the intermittent GitHub API staleness, which only occurs on a real runner at roughly 1 run in 7. The fix is proven in logic and observed in production, never 'verified' locally.

steps.name: Detect the current run anywhere on the page, not only where the count reaches
steps.description:
TDD execution — fixes a false-positive build failure found by probing the committed module.

**The defect.** `countBuildsToday` breaks out of the per-page loop at the first run older than `todayStart`. `sawCurrentRun` is only evaluated on runs the loop actually reaches, so a current run sitting *below* a newer pre-midnight run is never examined — the function concludes the listing is stale and `generateVersion` throws. This happens on a **re-run of an older workflow run**: a re-run keeps its original `created_at`, so it is not at the top of the listing.

Probed against the committed module with `now = 2026-09-22T10:00:00Z`, `ref = refs/heads/main`:

| Scenario | Current run | Result |
|---|---|---|
| normal push today | id 999 created today, newest | OK `v26.9.22.4` |
| re-run of yesterday's NEWEST run | id 201 created 09-21T18:00Z, the first pre-midnight entry | OK `v26.9.22.3` |
| **re-run of a 2-day-old run** | **id 101 created 09-20T08:00Z, below run 201** | **THROWS** |
| first run of the day, alone | id 999 created today | OK `v26.9.22.1` |
| stale page (Bug #6068) | id 999 absent entirely | THROWS — correct |

Only the third row is wrong. The listing there is perfectly fresh and contains the current run; the function simply never looked at it.

**RED phase** — add ONE test to `.github/scripts/generate-version.test.mjs`, alongside the existing five, which must all keep passing untouched:

`counts today's builds when the current run is a re-run from an earlier day` — `listRuns` returns, in descending `created_at` order: three runs from today, then a run from yesterday, then the current run from two days ago. `runId` is the two-day-old run. Expect it to RESOLVE with `buildCount === 3` and a version of `v26.9.22.3` — NOT to throw. Run `node --test '.github/scripts/'` and confirm this new test fails against the current module while the other five still pass.

**GREEN phase** — in `.github/scripts/generate-version.mjs`, make the freshness check independent of the counting loop's break: for each page fetched, test whether the page contains `runId` at all, rather than only testing the runs the counting loop walks past. Keep the same loose `String(a) === String(b)` comparison. Do NOT change the counting itself — the break stays exactly where it is, and `buildCount` must be identical in every scenario. This is a strictly wider freshness check: a page containing the current run is fresh with respect to that run no matter where the run sits.

**Verification** — all 6 tests pass. Re-run the probe script at `/tmp/claude-1000/-storage-repos-Lighthouse/1994d44c-2593-4990-b6a5-c549bc202fa0/scratchpad/probe-rerun.mjs` with `node` and confirm rows A, B, D are unchanged, E still throws (that is Bug #6068 being caught), and C now resolves to `v26.9.22.3`.

**COMMIT phase** — `fix(ci): look for the current run across the whole page`.
steps.scenario_name: Re-run of an older workflow run must not be mistaken for a stale listing
red_to_green_tests: counts today's builds when the current run is a re-run from an earlier day
criteria: A sixth test exists covering a re-run whose created_at places it below a newer pre-midnight run.
That test was confirmed FAILING against the unmodified module before the fix, and the failure was a thrown 'Refusing to emit a version', not an import or stub error.
After the fix all 6 tests pass.
The five pre-existing tests are byte-unchanged — `git diff` on the test file shows only the added test.
The freshness check tests each fetched page for runId independently of the counting loop's break.
The counting logic is unchanged: the break stays put and buildCount is identical in every probed scenario.
Probe re-run confirms A/B/D unchanged, E still throws, C now resolves.
Conventional commit, scope `ci`.
